quote: Okay. Actually, it's been actually, it's been forty years, not thirty.
stewart_read: A customer who volunteers a self-correction on tenure length (40 vs 30 years) is a strong 'we'll be here forever' signal — extremely long tenure homeowners are prime solar candidates because payback horizon isn't a concern. Rep acknowledged it warmly but did not anchor on it later in the pitch.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to flag long-tenure answers as a value signal to reinforce later — e.g., tie it to the appointment framing ('since you're not going anywhere, this pays for itself many times over').

quote: I just wanna ask my supervisor a question. Would you mind just waiting here for a minute?
stewart_read: The rep places the customer on hold for roughly a minute with no stated reason, and the customer's confused 'What?' at 04:52 after the silence shows the hold cost clarity. This is an emergent pattern not yet named in a specific schema slot — the schema's non_standard_scenario_hold definition is calibrated to off-grid/battery/mobile-home cases, and here the trigger (a geographic service-area question, clarified at 05:19-05:40) is different but structurally similar: rep needed a ruling before proceeding.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive read: rep simply didn't know how to handle an edge case and stalled rather than smoothly transitioning. Strategic read: rep was intentionally protecting the customer's time by verifying eligibility before continuing rather than continuing a doomed pitch — but the lack of any explanation to the customer during the hold undercuts this reading.
coaching_implication: If holds are necessary, coach the rep to tell the customer specifically what's being checked ('just confirming your area is inside our service region') rather than leaving her blind for a full minute.

quote: So it looks like you're just a tiny, tiny, tiny bit out of our bounds.
stewart_read: This is a distinct geographic/service-area ambiguity, separate from the credit qualifier that comes later at 05:46-06:02 — the rep is unclear here on whether the customer's address falls inside Ion's service territory, and resolves it a few lines later ('Yeah. It looks like I am good.') without ever explaining to the customer what 'bounds' meant.
coaching_implication: The vague 'out of our bounds' language could alarm a customer who is trying to determine legitimacy. Coach toward a cleaner statement once resolved: 'good news, you're inside our service area.'

stewart_read: This is a benign clarifying question from the customer about the credit threshold number itself, not an objection. The rep answers directly ('670 or above') and the customer self-reports 'It should be around that' — standard self-reported-credit handling per the schema's own open policy question on whether stated credit should gate the appointment.
coaching_implication: No coaching action needed here directly, but flag for the floor-wide open question: is self-reported 'around 670' sufficient to pass qualification, or should ambiguous self-reports be passed through to the closer's actual credit pull per qualifiers.credit_qualifier.spencer_operator_note?

quote: Well, I've you know, I have been checking it around, you know, you know, and none of that. My electric bill keeps going up.
stewart_read: The customer gives both an interest reason (rising bills) and, moments later, a specific bill range ($500-700/month, all-electric). The rep acknowledges sympathetically ('Oh my goodness') but never flips this into an emotional alignment-against-the-utility statement or ties it back to the appointment's value.
coaching_implication: Classic capture-without-flip. Coach the rep to use a line like 'so a $700 bill some months — that's money going straight to BGE with nothing to show for it, right?' before moving to the qualifier questions.

quote: Yeah. So what we could do is, I can just send you a text message. And then whenever you get home today, if you could just send me a photo of that,
stewart_read: The call ends on a bill-collection logistics plan with no appointment date or time ever proposed. There is no button_up sequence at all — no day/time, no hour-block framing, no 'is that fair?' handshake.
alternative_hypothesis: Strategic read: since this appears to be a paid lead requiring the bill before booking (per lead_types_and_bill_collection_rules), it's plausible the rep intends to book only after the bill photo arrives. But the rep never says this explicitly to the customer or frames a follow-up call time, so the call still ends procedurally unanchored.
coaching_implication: Even when bill collection must precede booking, the rep should state the next step explicitly: 'once I get that photo, I'll call you back today to lock in a time with our specialist.' Coach toward always closing with a stated next contact point, not just 'we will keep in touch.'
